name: Wide Playmakers 4-3-3

slots.why: Sweeper keeper is an extra passer in build-up and covers the space behind a higher line.
Support full-back gives the width the creators no longer give.
Ball-playing defender starts moves with passes into midfield.
Central defender who defends while his partner plays. Cover is the alternate.
Support full-back on the right, providing width there too.
Ball-winning midfielder wins the ball back and covers for the creators, who do little defending.
Box-to-box midfielder supports the press and runs beyond the forward.
Supporting central midfielder links the defence with the creators.
Trequartista starts on the left and roams freely to find space between the lines; he does not defend.
Advanced playmaker starts on the right and moves inside to create from the half-space.
Pressing forward (Attack) starts the press and runs in behind, doing the work the creators do not.

description: A 4-3-3 with two creative players starting wide, one a trequartista who roams and one an advanced playmaker, supported by a pressing forward and a strong midfield.
whyGood: Two creators starting from wide positions are hard to mark, and the pressing forward, ball-winner and box-to-box midfielder cover the work they do not do.
whyThisShape: Starting the creators wide rather than in the middle means opposing central midfielders cannot easily mark them, and each drifts inside to receive between the lines. The pressing forward, ball-winner and box-to-box midfielder do the defensive work for them, and the full-backs supply the width they leave.
whenToUse: When your best creative players are wingers or attacking midfielders rather than central playmakers, against sides that defend in a mid-block.
whenNotToUse: Against teams that press hard on the full-backs, since the full-backs supply all the width; and when the creators cannot be protected by a strong midfield.

instructionRationale.Shorter Passing: Keeps the ball in short passes, which is how the creators link with the midfield.
instructionRationale.Work Ball Into Box: Patient movement of the ball until one of the creators finds the pass that opens the defence.
instructionRationale.Counter-Press: Presses at once after losing the ball, led by the pressing forward and ball-winner.
instructionRationale.Higher Line of Engagement: Presses higher up the pitch to keep the play in the opponent's half.
instructionRationale.Standard Defensive Line: A balanced line keeps the defence compact.

keyRequirements: Two creative players who can play wide
A pressing forward with high work rate
